definitions.explanation: A small, round, hard piece of candy meant to be sucked rather than chewed. A traditional Japanese confection that comes in various flavors.

examples.english: To suck on a hard candy.

examples.japanese: {おばあちゃん|おばあちゃん}がいつも{飴玉|あめだま}をくれた。
examples.english: Grandma always gave me hard candies.

examples.japanese: {喉|のど}が{痛|いた}いときは{飴玉|あめだま}を{一|ひと}つ{口|くち}に{入|い}れると{楽|らく}になる。
examples.english: When your throat hurts, popping a hard candy in your mouth helps.

notes:
USAGE:
The word combines {飴|あめ} (candy) and {玉|たま} (ball), describing the round shape. While {飴|あめ} can refer to any kind of candy or sweets in general, {飴玉|あめだま} specifically refers to the hard, round type.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {飴玉|あめだま}をなめる (to suck on a candy)
- {飴玉|あめだま}をしゃぶる (to suck on a candy)
- {飴玉|あめだま}を{配|くば}る (to hand out candies)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {飴|あめ}: candy, sweets — broader term
- キャンディー: candy — loanword, more modern feel
